corrections.text: The summary says the May 2026 Stainless shutdown 'shows what two customers did after a hosted service closed'. Only Google links its move (partnering with Speakeasy to open-source its generator suite) to the shutdown, in its own blog post, without naming Stainless. For Cloudflare, the link between the Stainless wind-down and Forge is The New Stack's reading ('goes some way toward explaining why Cloudflare is making Forge open source'); Cloudflare's authors do not name Stainless, and Forge was released in September, months after the May events. The body of the article states this; the summary and Overview do not.

The article's account of Factory's HumanLayer acquisition rests on a single outlet, The New Stack, whose article states: 'TNS owner Insight Partners is an investor in: Factory.' The article does not mention this relationship. The New Stack's HumanLayer report also refers to 'the transition' for the hosted service without giving its length; the article reports only that no shutdown date had been set.

The article says SiliconANGLE reported that Conductor will delete the local app's user data 'when it shuts down in early 2027'. SiliconANGLE says local copies of the Mac app keep working until early 2027, when new models and critical bug fixes stop arriving and Conductor deletes the app's user data; the phrase 'when the application shuts down' is InfoWorld's.
